target_customer: Homebuyers who want custom homes, with builders and land developers as supply partners
problem: Designing and building a custom house is slow and fragmented; Atmos moved design and planning online and connected buyers with builders.
business_model: Marketplace and design service taking fees on custom homes designed and built through partner builders
product_category: Proptech custom home design and building platform

founders.name: Nicholas Donahue
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2020 and 2025: from a homebuilding family, built a Burning Man art installation and an open source VR headset; Forbes 30 Under 30 per YC page.

founders.name: Trent Hedge
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page as cofounder at Atmos.

founders.name: Matthew Rastovac
previous_startups: Respell (CEO, acquired by Salesforce per YC page)

exit.reason: Donahue said it became an extremely operational business and that higher interest rates left clients unable to afford homes they had spent months designing

technical_complexity.rationale: Software for home design and pricing plus coordination of real construction; the stated goal of replacing human designers was never fully reached.

defensibility.rationale: Execution depended on local builder relationships and human designers. No data or regulatory moat is described.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent response found. Rate hikes after 2022 hurt buyers, which ended the business.

market_need_then: Donahue's family background in homebuilding and high demand for custom homes during 2020 supported the pitch; the 2022 Series A coverage describes an online marketplace linking buyers with builders and land developers.

branding.domain_note: Used buildatmos.com rather than atmos.com; no purchase details found.
branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage of the TikTok star Josh Richards investment and Forbes 30 Under 30 recognition of the founders; no sign of brand driven community.

brand_strength.rationale: Founder and investor press helped awareness, but no source shows the brand itself drove growth, and the name is shared with a large gas utility that dominates search results.

outcome_analysis: Atmos raised about 18.5 million dollars across three recorded rounds, led by Khosla, and completed roughly 50 homes and designed about 200 million dollars of projects. The founder said it became operationally heavy, never fully replaced human designers, and was hit when higher interest rates priced out clients, and it shut down around March 2025.
notes: Company website returned HTTP 503. The 2020 June round of 2M is the founder's figure to TechCrunch. The 2022 Series A of 12.5M is reported by WRAL TechWire, Duke Capital Partners and an AOL copy of TechCrunch; I read these only as search summaries. Totals conflict: TechCrunch 2025 says 20M, CB Insights 20.84M over 8 rounds, Employbl 18.655M, my recorded rounds sum to 18.5M, so rounds may be missing. The YC page cites a Forbes 25M valuation for October 2020, which I did not open and so did not record. Shutdown month is approximate (TechCrunch says about nine months before December 2025). No dated competitor source found: TechCrunch 2020 names none and CB Insights lists Homebound, Higharc and Welcome Homes without dates.
